name: Stocks
experienceSuitability: More suitable for investors who understand market and company risk
advantages: Direct ownership exposure to listed companies
Can be bought or sold during market hours
risks: Prices can fall sharply
Individual companies can underperform or fail
limitations: Requires research and ongoing risk awareness
No assured income or capital protection
description: Shares represent ownership in listed companies. Their value can change significantly with company results, market conditions, and investor sentiment.

name: Mutual Funds
liquidity: Medium to high, varies by fund
experienceSuitability: Available for different experience levels; fund selection matters
advantages: Professionally managed pooled investments
Wide range of strategies and underlying assets
risks: Risk depends on the scheme's holdings
Market-linked funds can lose value
limitations: Fees, exit loads, and redemption rules vary by scheme
Past performance does not establish future results
description: A mutual fund pools money from investors and invests according to a stated scheme. Risk, liquidity, fees, and suitable holding period differ across schemes.

name: Exchange-Traded Funds
experienceSuitability: Requires understanding of the fund's holdings and trading price
advantages: Trades on an exchange during market hours
Can provide diversified exposure in one instrument
risks: Market and underlying-asset risk
Trading price may differ from net asset value
limitations: Liquidity and costs vary by ETF
Some products track volatile or concentrated assets
description: An ETF holds a basket of assets and trades on an exchange. Its risk depends on what it owns, how it tracks its index, and market liquidity.

name: Index Funds
experienceSuitability: A simple structure, but index and tracking risks still matter
advantages: Rules-based exposure to a chosen market index
Typically diversified across index constituents
risks: Follows market declines in its index
Concentration risk depends on index composition
limitations: Does not aim to avoid weak constituents
Tracking difference and fees vary
description: An index fund seeks to follow a market index. It does not remove market risk, and an index's sector and company mix can change its risk profile.

name: Large Cap Funds
experienceSuitability: May be easier to understand than smaller-company funds, but remains market-linked
advantages: Exposure to larger established companies
Can spread investment across multiple holdings
risks: Equity markets can fall
Large companies can still underperform
limitations: No assured return or capital protection
Fund holdings and costs vary
description: Large-cap funds invest mainly in larger companies. They remain equity investments and may be unsuitable for money needed in the near term.

name: Mid Cap Funds
experienceSuitability: More suitable for investors comfortable with larger price swings
advantages: Exposure to mid-sized listed companies
Can complement a broader diversified portfolio
risks: Can be more volatile than large-company exposure
Liquidity and company-specific risks
limitations: May experience deep or prolonged declines
Not designed for short-term spending needs
description: Mid-cap funds invest in medium-sized companies. They can fluctuate substantially and generally require a long investment horizon.

name: Small Cap Funds
experienceSuitability: Usually suited only to experienced investors who can tolerate high volatility
advantages: Exposure to smaller listed businesses
May diversify a portfolio with an appropriate risk budget
risks: High volatility and liquidity risk
Smaller companies may face greater business uncertainty
limitations: Large losses are possible
Not suitable for emergency or near-term funds
description: Small-cap funds invest in smaller companies and can be highly volatile. Suitability depends on risk capacity, time horizon, and diversification.

name: Hybrid Funds
riskLevel: Low to high, varies by allocation
experienceSuitability: Accessible to different experience levels; allocation and scheme rules matter
advantages: Combines more than one asset class
Allocation is managed within the scheme
risks: Market risk remains in the underlying assets
Risk changes with the scheme's allocation
limitations: Asset mix and rebalancing rules vary
Not all hybrid funds provide capital stability
description: Hybrid funds combine asset classes such as equity and debt. The balance, risk, and liquidity depend on the particular scheme.

name: Debt Funds
riskLevel: Low to moderate, varies by fund
experienceSuitability: Understand credit quality, interest-rate sensitivity, and fund duration
advantages: Exposure to debt instruments
Multiple duration and credit-quality strategies are available
risks: Credit risk and interest-rate risk
NAV can fall; returns are not guaranteed
limitations: Not the same as a bank deposit
Tax treatment and redemption rules may differ
description: Debt funds invest in fixed-income instruments. Their value can change with interest rates, issuer credit quality, and liquidity conditions.

name: Liquid Funds
experienceSuitability: Relatively straightforward, but not equivalent to a guaranteed bank deposit
advantages: Designed for short-term cash management
Generally offers redemption access subject to scheme terms
risks: Credit, liquidity, and reinvestment risk remain
Value and access are not guaranteed
limitations: Not covered by deposit insurance
Redemption timelines and limits vary by scheme
description: Liquid funds invest in short-maturity debt instruments. They may be considered for short-term cash needs, but are not risk-free or guaranteed.

name: Corporate Bonds
experienceSuitability: Requires checking issuer credit quality, maturity, and market liquidity
advantages: Can provide scheduled interest payments
Different issuers and maturities are available
risks: Issuer may delay or default on payments
Bond price can fall when interest rates change
limitations: Secondary-market liquidity may be limited
Credit rating is an opinion, not a guarantee
description: A corporate bond is debt issued by a company. Payment depends on the issuer's ability to meet its obligations and on the bond's terms.

name: Government Securities
riskLevel: Low credit risk, market risk remains
experienceSuitability: Understand maturity, price changes, and how the security is purchased
advantages: Issued by the Government of India
Some securities provide scheduled interest payments
risks: Market value may change before maturity
Inflation can reduce purchasing power
limitations: Early sale price is not assured
Access and minimum amounts vary by route and security
description: Government securities are debt obligations issued by the Government of India. They have market and inflation risk, especially if sold before maturity.

name: Fixed Deposits
liquidity: Low to medium, premature withdrawal rules apply
experienceSuitability: Straightforward to understand; compare the issuer and terms
advantages: Known deposit terms at the time of booking
Tenures and payout options may be available
risks: Issuer risk and inflation risk
Premature withdrawal may reduce interest
limitations: Deposit insurance, where applicable, has limits
Rates and terms vary by institution and can change
description: A fixed deposit holds money with a bank or other institution for a chosen term. Protection and early withdrawal rules depend on the provider and applicable limits.

name: Recurring Deposits
liquidity: Low to medium, early closure rules apply
experienceSuitability: Straightforward recurring saving structure
advantages: Supports regular contributions
Terms are set by the institution
risks: Issuer and inflation risk
Missed installments may affect terms
limitations: Early closure rules and penalties vary
May not keep pace with inflation
description: A recurring deposit accepts regular contributions for a fixed period. Terms, payout, and early closure rules depend on the institution.

name: Physical Gold
experienceSuitability: Understand purity, pricing, and safe storage
advantages: A tangible asset
Can diversify exposure across asset types
risks: Price volatility and buy/sell spread
Theft, damage, or purity risk
limitations: Storage and making charges may apply
Does not generate regular income
description: Physical gold is a tangible commodity. Its price fluctuates and the investor must consider purity, storage, and transaction costs.

name: Gold ETFs
experienceSuitability: Requires a demat/trading route and understanding of market pricing
advantages: Exchange-traded exposure to gold prices
No physical storage at home
risks: Gold-price volatility
Tracking, market-liquidity, and fund expenses
limitations: Does not provide regular income
Trading price and underlying value may differ
description: A gold ETF seeks to track gold exposure and trades on an exchange. Value, liquidity, tracking, and fees vary.

name: Silver
experienceSuitability: Requires tolerance for commodity volatility and product-specific costs
advantages: Provides exposure to a distinct commodity
May diversify other asset exposures
risks: Commodity prices can be highly volatile
Industrial demand and currency can affect prices
limitations: No regular income
Physical handling, storage, and transaction costs may apply
description: Silver can be held physically or through market products. It is a volatile commodity and may not suit short-term or essential funds.

name: Sovereign Gold Bonds
liquidity: Low to medium; exit conditions apply
experienceSuitability: Understand issue availability, holding period, and exit rules
advantages: Government-issued gold-linked instrument when available
No need to store physical gold
risks: Value is linked to gold prices
Selling before the applicable exit date can be difficult or at a discount
limitations: New issues may not always be available
Maturity and early redemption rules apply
description: Sovereign Gold Bonds are government securities linked to gold prices and issued under specific terms. Availability, maturity, and exit conditions should be checked.

name: Real Estate Investment Trusts
experienceSuitability: Requires understanding of property, tenant, and interest-rate exposure
advantages: Exchange-listed exposure to income-producing real estate
Can diversify listed investments
risks: Property occupancy, valuation, and interest-rate risk
Distribution amounts can change
limitations: Market price may move independently of property values
Liquidity and tax treatment vary
description: A REIT owns or finances income-generating real estate. Units trade on an exchange and both prices and distributions can change.

name: Infrastructure Investment Trusts
experienceSuitability: Requires understanding of infrastructure assets and financing risks
advantages: Listed exposure to infrastructure assets
May provide distributions under trust terms
risks: Project, regulatory, financing, and interest-rate risk
Distributions can vary
limitations: Unit liquidity may be limited
Asset valuations and tax treatment require review
description: An InvIT holds infrastructure assets or related investments. Outcomes depend on operating performance, regulation, leverage, and market conditions.

name: Public Provident Fund
liquidity: Low; lock-in and withdrawal rules apply
experienceSuitability: Accessible to beginners who can commit to a long lock-in
advantages: Government-backed small-savings scheme
Long-term disciplined saving structure
risks: Liquidity is restricted by scheme rules
Inflation can affect long-term purchasing power
limitations: Long lock-in with conditional partial access
Contribution and tax rules can change
description: PPF is a long-term government small-savings scheme with defined contribution, maturity, and withdrawal rules. Current rules should be verified before investing.

name: National Pension System
experienceSuitability: Designed for retirement saving; understand allocation and withdrawal rules
advantages: Retirement-focused account structure
Multiple investment and allocation choices
risks: Market risk depends on selected assets
Retirement corpus and annuity outcomes are not guaranteed
limitations: Withdrawal and exit rules restrict access
Annuity terms and tax treatment require review
description: NPS is a retirement-focused investment system with asset allocation and withdrawal rules. Returns and retirement income are not guaranteed.

name: International Stocks
experienceSuitability: Requires understanding of foreign markets, currency, tax, and access rules
advantages: Exposure to companies outside the home market
Can diversify geographic exposure
risks: Market, currency, geopolitical, and regulatory risk
Cross-border tax and settlement complexity
limitations: Access, costs, and rules vary by platform and jurisdiction
No assured return or income
description: International stocks represent ownership in companies listed outside India. Investors face both share-price and currency risk, plus cross-border rules and costs.

name: International ETFs
experienceSuitability: Requires understanding of the fund's region, holdings, currency, and trading route
advantages: Access to a basket of non-domestic assets
Can diversify across regions or markets
risks: Underlying market and currency risk
Foreign market hours and liquidity can affect pricing
limitations: Access and costs depend on product and platform
Tax, tracking, and regulatory rules vary
description: An international ETF tracks or holds assets from outside India. Risk depends on its holdings, currency exposure, market liquidity, and applicable access rules.
